newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon says "mafia" behind German toxic shipment.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon says "mafia" behind German toxic shipment.

text.p: Lebanon is investigating an illegal shipment of some 680 tonnes of German plastic toxic waste seized at Beirut port and a cabinet minister said on Monday an "international waste mafia" was behind the deal.

Environment Minister Pierre Pharaon told a news conference the Lebanese government would ask Germany to take back the 36 containers containing the waste, which have been held at Beirut port since August 4.
"The containers will not under any circumstances enter Lebanon," Pharaon said.
"The Lebanese government has seized the containers and is suing the importers including some Lebanese and an international mafia," he added.
The Lebanese importer of the waste and a customs agent have been detained and four environment ministry employees are being questioned in connection with the case, judicial sources said.
They said Lebanon had been notified by Interpol on August 13 that a suspect shipment concealed as "plastic granules" might have entered Beirut port from Germany via Holland.
Judicial authorities seized the shipment and asked the environment ministry on August 27 to test the material.
Pharaon said experts delegated by the ministry had tested the shipment and submitted a report on September 19 that said "the waste was polluted and cannot be recycled".

The report said the shipment included plastic containers and industrial and chemical waste which cause skin and eye irritation. Also included were pieces of carbonised plastic which cannot be recycled, they added.
Judicial sources said initial questioning of the Lebanese importer, who was detained last Friday, revealed that he had imported the waste under a deal with a Jordanian businessman in Germany.
The importer had told the prosecutors the deal was brokered by his brother who lives in Russia. An agent for the Jordanian businessman at Beirut port, was also detained in connection with the case.
The judicial sources said the agent had sold two containers to a local recycling firm for $14,000, but the firm withheld payment after seeing they did not contain plastic granules.

Prosecutor General Adnan Addoum will discuss the issue on Tuesday with the German commercial attache in Lebanon and will ask Lebanon's foreign ministry to raise the matter with the German foreign ministry, the sources added.
